title: Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact
blurb: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union sign a non-aggression pact with secret protocols to divide Eastern Europe. The diplomatic fuse for Poland is lit.

title: Germany invades Poland
blurb: Without a formal declaration of war, German forces cross into Poland at dawn. Blitzkrieg meets a two-front nightmare when the Soviets invade from the east on the 17th.

title: Britain & France declare war
blurb: Chamberlain’s broadcast ends the illusions of Munich. The European war is official—yet for months the Western Front barely stirs.

title: Soviet invasion of Poland
blurb: The Red Army crosses Poland’s eastern border under the secret pact. Poland is erased between two totalitarian partners.

title: Winter War begins
blurb: The USSR attacks Finland. Tiny Finnish forces bloody the Red Army through the winter; the peace of March 1940 costs Finland territory but not independence.

title: Denmark & Norway invaded
blurb: Weserübung seizes Denmark in hours and contests Norway for two months. The Allies evacuate; Churchill becomes PM mid-crisis.

title: Fall of the Low Countries
blurb: Germany drives through the Ardennes, bypassing the Maginot Line. Rotterdam is bombed; the Netherlands surrender in days.

title: Dunkirk evacuation
blurb: Operation Dynamo lifts ~338,000 Allied troops from the beaches. A military disaster becomes a propaganda deliverance—and Britain fights on.

title: Germans enter Paris
blurb: An open city falls without a fight. The swastika rises over the Eiffel Tower; France’s Third Republic is days from collapse.

title: French armistice
blurb: Hitler forces the signing in the same railway carriage where Germany capitulated in 1918. Vichy governs the unoccupied south; occupation divides France.

title: Battle of Britain begins
blurb: The Luftwaffe tries to smash the RAF ahead of invasion. Radar, fighter production, and pilot skill deny Germany the sky.

title: The Blitz begins
blurb: Night bombing shifts to cities. Fifty-seven consecutive nights hammer London; Coventry, Liverpool, and others burn. Civilian will holds.

title: Italy invades Greece
blurb: Mussolini’s poorly prepared offensive stalls in the mountains. Greek counterattacks push into Albania—drawing German attention south.

title: Yugoslavia & Greece invaded
blurb: Germany overruns Yugoslavia in days and Greece soon after. Crete falls by air in May—costly for German paratroops.

title: Operation Barbarossa
blurb: Three million Axis troops smash into the Soviet Union—the largest land invasion in history. Stalin is stunned; the character of the war turns genocidal in the East.

title: Siege of Leningrad begins
blurb: The city is cut off. Nearly 900 days of starvation, cold, and shelling follow—one of the war’s longest and cruelest sieges.

title: Kiev falls
blurb: The Wehrmacht completes a vast encirclement. Hundreds of thousands of Soviet troops are captured—and the road opens toward further atrocity in Ukraine.

title: Drive on Moscow (Typhoon)
blurb: Operation Typhoon aims to take the Soviet capital before winter. Mud, then frost, then a Soviet reserve army will stop it.

title: Soviet Moscow counteroffensive
blurb: Fresh Siberian divisions and winter smash the frozen German spearheads. The myth of Wehrmacht invincibility cracks.

title: Germany declares war on the US
blurb: Four days after Pearl Harbor, Hitler declares war on the United States—bringing American industry fully into the European struggle.

title: Wannsee Conference
blurb: Senior Nazi officials coordinate the logistics of the ‘Final Solution.’ This site treats the Holocaust soberly and separately from campaign scrubbing—see the note in About.

title: Rommel drives on Egypt
blurb: The Desert Fox breaks the Gazala line; Tobruk falls in June. Egypt—and the Suez—suddenly look reachable.

title: Battle of Stalingrad opens
blurb: House-by-house fighting begins on the Volga. What starts as a city fight becomes the war’s decisive German catastrophe.

title: Dieppe Raid
blurb: A costly Allied reconnaissance-in-force on the French coast. Lessons in landing craft, armor, and air cover will shape Normandy.

title: Second El Alamein
blurb: Montgomery’s Eighth Army breaks Rommel. Churchill: ‘Before Alamein we never had a victory. After Alamein we never had a defeat.’

title: Operation Torch
blurb: American and British forces land in French North Africa. Vichy resistance fades; the Axis is soon squeezed from east and west.

title: Operation Uranus
blurb: Soviet pincers smash through weak Romanian flanks and encircle the German Sixth Army. The trap closes.

title: Sixth Army surrenders
blurb: Field Marshal Paulus capitulates. Roughly 90,000 Axis troops march into captivity; maybe 5–6,000 ever see home. The strategic initiative in the East passes to the USSR.

title: Goebbels’ Total War speech
blurb: At the Sportpalast, Goebbels asks ‘Do you want total war?’ The crowd roars yes. Propaganda tries to paper over Stalingrad.

title: Axis surrender in Tunisia
blurb: A quarter-million Axis troops lay down arms. Africa is cleared; the Mediterranean becomes an Allied highway toward Sicily.

title: Battle of Kursk
blurb: The largest tank battle in history. Germany’s last major strategic offensive in the East dies in Soviet defenses and counterstrokes.

title: Allies invade Sicily
blurb: Husky lands Anglo-American forces on Sicily. Within weeks Mussolini is deposed; Italy’s Fascist regime cracks.

title: Allies land in mainland Italy
blurb: Italy surrenders; Germany seizes the north and digs in. Salerno is nearly thrown back into the sea. A long, bitter slog up the peninsula begins.

title: Tehran Conference
blurb: Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin meet. Overlord is locked in for 1944; the shape of the postwar world starts to be bargained.

title: Anzio landing
blurb: A flanking landing meant to break the Gustav Line stalls into a bloody beachhead. Rome will wait until June.

title: Leningrad siege lifted
blurb: After 872 days, the corridor opens for good. The human cost is almost beyond measure—estimates near a million civilian dead.

title: Allies enter Rome
blurb: The first Axis capital falls—two days before Normandy steals the headlines. German forces withdraw in good order to the Gothic Line.

title: D-Day — Normandy landings
blurb: Overlord: five beaches, airborne drops, the greatest amphibious assault ever mounted. A foothold in Fortress Europe is won by nightfall—at terrible cost on Omaha.

title: Operation Bagration
blurb: On the anniversary of Barbarossa, the Red Army annihilates Army Group Centre. The map of the East rewrites itself in weeks.

title: July 20 plot
blurb: Stauffenberg’s bomb fails to kill Hitler. The purge that follows guts the conservative resistance inside the Wehrmacht.

title: Warsaw Uprising
blurb: The Polish Home Army rises as the Red Army nears. Stalin’s forces halt across the Vistula; the city is destroyed over 63 days.

title: Invasion of southern France
blurb: Operation Dragoon races up the Rhône. German Army Group G retreats; France is liberated from two directions.

title: Liberation of Paris
blurb: French 2nd Armored and US forces enter; Resistance rises. De Gaulle walks the Champs-Élysées. The city’s cultural weight makes the moment electric.

title: Market Garden
blurb: A bridge too far. Ambitious airborne thrusts into the Netherlands fail to seize the Rhine crossing at Arnhem.

title: Battle of the Bulge
blurb: Hitler’s last major western offensive punches a salient through thin US lines. Bastogne holds; fuel and air power decide the rest.

title: Vistula–Oder offensive
blurb: Zhukov and Konev surge from the Vistula to the Oder in two weeks—stopping 70 km from Berlin. East Prussia is cut off.

title: Yalta Conference
blurb: The Big Three carve occupation zones and argue Poland’s future. The Cold War’s outline is visible if you squint.

title: Dresden firebombed
blurb: RAF and USAAF raids create a firestorm in a crowded refugee city. The morality of area bombing remains bitterly contested.

title: Remagen bridge seized
blurb: US troops find the Ludendorff Bridge still standing and cross the Rhine. A temporary miracle accelerates the western advance.

title: Battle of Berlin begins
blurb: Soviet armies assault the capital. Street fighting, Hitler’s bunker, and the final collapse of Nazi authority follow.

title: Elbe Day — link-up
blurb: US and Soviet patrols meet on the Elbe. Germany is cut in two; photographers stage the handshake for history.

title: Hitler dead
blurb: Hitler suicides as Soviet troops close on the Reich Chancellery. Dönitz inherits a wreck for a few days of ‘government.’

title: Berlin falls
blurb: The Berlin garrison surrenders. The Red Banner over the Reichstag becomes the iconic image of victory in Europe.

title: German surrender signed
blurb: Jodl signs unconditional surrender at Eisenhower’s HQ. A second ceremony in Berlin follows; VE Day is celebrated on the 8th (and the 9th in Moscow).

title: VE Day
blurb: Crowds fill Whitehall and the Champs-Élysées. The European war is over. The Pacific war—and the atomic age—still wait.
